income_claim.rule: present exactly when every income entry is null

words: DB-b-287 (round 148, workstream PUBWRITE) makes the publisher and the Cottonwood publish handler write what series contract 0.3.1 declares. The publisher is version 0.3.0. When every income entry of a series is null, build_series writes income_claim = absent as the last key, after the unreported-days pair; a series with income null on some days and numbers on others is refused, and numeric income writes no claim. build_manifest takes an optional calendar_source, appended last and accepting only the two contract words; validate_against_contract grades both new keys against the contract. The handler reads which calendar answered, writes calendar_source with its manifest, and refuses by name a contract that does not name either new key before any S3 call. The 49 Financial series stays byte-identical to the base commit's on the checker's all-numeric fixture, and its manifest differs only in publisher_version. NOT PROVEN: that the deployed functions write any of this (a later code-update pair), that the page reads income_claim or calendar_source, and that live 49 Financial gold with mixed null income is handled as the base handled it.
